rows: The front pair of eyes is sharp but narrow. Each front retina is about 2 degrees wide and 21 degrees high, and the spider moves it to scan.
The side eyes cover nearly the whole ring around the spider, a wide and blurry view that catches movement.
The front retinas scan side to side about once every second and a bit, and twist about 20 to 30 degrees each way. They rest on a still target for several seconds.
The side eyes answer to movement and ignore a still scene. A light that only switches on and off calls no turn.
The front eyes see ultraviolet and green. The colours a person sees are made from those two classes, so reds look dim.
The sharp middle, the blur, the glow, the sound response and the gaze weights are the app's own drawing, and no record gives their values.

claims.how: Phidippus johnsoni principal eye acuity of 3.8 cycles per degree, from a 0.13 degree receptor angle.
The front zone takes the same 3.8 cycles per degree from the principal eye of Phidippus johnsoni.
Principal retina subtends about 21 degrees high by 2 degrees wide in object space.
Records give near 300 to near 360 degrees for the whole animal's secondary eyes; the app sets 300 within that range, allowing for the blind gap behind.
A 15 degree saccade is complete within 0.1 s, giving at least 150 degrees a second; base 40 ms and 4 ms per degree are the app's fit to that figure.
Tracking was tested below 10 degrees a second.
Reduced detection after a cue lasts in the order of 5 seconds.
Side eyes respond only to movement; the gate value itself is the app's choice, so it is graded i.
